{"code": "import pandas as pd

data = pd.read_csv('data/trial.csv')

# Step 1: Deduplicate on patient_id, keeping highest sample_seq per patient
# This is required by the data dictionary: highest sample_seq supersedes earlier rows
print(f'Patient ID duplicates before dedup: {data["patient_id"].duplicated().sum()}')
data = data.sort_values('sample_seq', ascending=False).drop_duplicates(subset='patient_id', keep='first')
print(f'Patient ID duplicates after dedup: {data["patient_id"].duplicated().sum()}')

# Step 2: Correct assay_batch B values: divide by 10 to convert µg/L to ng/mL
# Batch A is already in ng/mL, so no change needed
print(f'Batch B count before correction: {(data["assay_batch"] == "B").sum()}')
data.loc[data['assay_batch'] == 'B', 'biomarker_final'] = data.loc[data['assay_batch'] == 'B', 'biomarker_final'] / 10
print(f'Batch B count after correction: {(data["assay_batch"] == "B").sum()}')

# Step 3: Compute mean biomarker_final across all patients (including those with baseline -999)
mean_biomarker_final = data['biomarker_final'].mean()
print(f'Mean biomarker_final (ng/mL): {mean_biomarker_final}')

# Print number of patients after deduplication
n_patients = data.shape[0]
print(f'Number of patients after deduplication: {n_patients}')

# Print number of batch B entries after correction
n_batch_b = (data['assay_batch'] == 'B').sum()
print(f'Number of batch B entries after correction: {n_batch_b}')"}
